title: Allowing Private Hire Car and Taxi Drivers to Install Passenger Facing Video Recorders with Audio Functions
what_it_is: Allowing Private Hire Car and Taxi Drivers to Install Passenger Facing Video Recorders with Audio Functions

sections.label: Taxi passenger-facing video recorders rules
sections.summary: LTA permits taxi and private hire car drivers to install passenger-facing video recorders with audio only with prior permission, at authorised centres, with access limited to investigation and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister of Transport)
sentences.text: Since 2019, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) has allowed taxi and private hire car drivers to install passenger-facing video recorders with audio functions in their vehicles, with prior permission from LTA, and only at LTA-authorised installation centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister of Transport)
sentences.text: To protect passengers' privacy and guard against misuse, recordings made by these devices can only be accessed for investigation and enforcement purposes, such as in fare-related disputes and by authorised Government personnel and LTA-authorised persons only.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister of Transport)
sentences.text: Vehicles with such devices must be affixed with a notice to inform passengers and passengers must also be informed by operators should such a vehicle be matched to them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister of Transport)
sentences.text: Taxi and private hire car drivers may not install and use unauthorised recording devices, such as their personal mobile phones, to record audio and/or video within their vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister of Transport)
sentences.text: In cases where drivers have been harassed by passengers who have used recording devices and shared these recordings online without the drivers' consent, drivers may seek recourse, including under the Protection from Harassment Act.
